concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Coulomb's law and superposition
concepts.description: Coulomb's law gives the magnitude of the force between two point charges as F = k|q1q2|/r^2 in vacuum. Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. For several charges, calculate each force on the target charge and add the force vectors; this is the superposition principle.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Ohm's law and resistance
concepts.description: For an ohmic conductor at fixed physical conditions, potential difference V is proportional to current I, so V = IR. Resistance measures opposition to current and is measured in ohms. The relation is a model for ohmic behavior; not every device has a linear V-I relationship.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
concepts.name: Photoelectric effect
concepts.description: In the photoelectric effect, light can eject electrons from a material when its frequency exceeds a threshold frequency. Einstein's relation is K_max = hf - φ, where φ is the work function. Increasing intensity at an above-threshold frequency increases the number of emitted electrons, while frequency controls the maximum kinetic energy in the ideal introductory model.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Capacitors in series and parallel
concepts.description: For capacitors in parallel, each has the same potential difference and equivalent capacitance is the sum. In series, each carries equal-magnitude charge and reciprocal capacitances add. These rules follow from the circuit connections.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Faraday’s law and Lenz’s law
concepts.description: An emf is induced when magnetic flux through a circuit changes. Faraday’s law gives ε = −dΦB/dt for one loop; the negative sign expresses Lenz’s law: induced effects oppose the change in flux that produced them.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Thin lenses and image formation
concepts.description: For a thin lens under the usual Cartesian sign convention, the lens equation is 1/f = 1/v − 1/u. Magnification is m = v/u. The signs of object distance, image distance, and focal length indicate the physical arrangement and image type.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Electric dipole and dipole moment
concepts.description: An electric dipole consists of equal and opposite charges separated by a distance. Its dipole moment points from negative to positive charge and has magnitude p=qd, where d is the separation. In a uniform electric field, the dipole experiences a torque tending to align p with the field.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Gauss law and symmetric charge distributions
concepts.description: Gauss law states that electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by ε₀. It is especially useful when charge distributions have spherical, cylindrical, or planar symmetry, allowing the field magnitude to be constant over useful parts of a Gaussian surface.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Emf and internal resistance
concepts.description: A real cell can be modelled as emf ε in series with internal resistance r. When it supplies current I, terminal voltage is V=ε−Ir. The emf is energy supplied per unit charge, while terminal voltage is the potential difference available at the external terminals.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Magnetic force on a moving charge
concepts.description: A charge q moving with velocity v in magnetic field B experiences force F=q(v×B), with magnitude |q|vB sinθ. The force is perpendicular to velocity and field, so it changes direction of motion but does no work in a static magnetic field.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: RMS value and AC power
concepts.description: For a sinusoidal alternating current, the rms value is the equivalent steady current that would produce the same average heating in a resistor. Irms=I₀/√2 and Vrms=V₀/√2. For a pure resistor, average power is Vrms Irms.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Mass defect and binding energy
concepts.description: The mass of a bound nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of its separated nucleons. The mass defect Δm corresponds to binding energy E=Δmc². Binding energy per nucleon helps compare nuclear stability, with a broad maximum among medium-mass nuclei.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Young double-slit interference
concepts.description: In Young’s double-slit experiment, coherent light from two slits produces alternating bright and dark fringes. For small angles, fringe width is β=λD/d, where λ is wavelength, D is screen distance, and d is slit separation. Increasing λ or D widens fringes; increasing d narrows them.

concepts.subject: Physics
concepts.name: Electromagnetic spectrum and wave properties
concepts.description: Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves of coupled electric and magnetic fields and can propagate through vacuum. In vacuum they travel at c; the spectrum is ordered by frequency or wavelength, with c=fλ. Higher frequency means shorter wavelength at fixed c.
